stories.title: Building an AI-ready workforce: How San Jac is helping Houston businesses upskill employees
stories.simple_summary: A school in Houston is teaching business employees how to use AI tools in their jobs. It's like a training class to help workers get comfortable with new technology.
stories.why_it_matters: If you own a small business, this shows that training programs exist to help your employees learn AI — which could make them more productive.

stories.title: US to press G20 on light-touch AI regulation
stories.simple_summary: The US government is asking other major countries to not create too many strict rules for AI. They want countries to regulate AI lightly rather than heavily.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and big tech companies — it won't directly affect how you use AI in your business right now.

stories.title: Fresno County school districts weigh benefits and risks of AI in classrooms
stories.simple_summary: Schools in Fresno County are thinking about whether to use AI in classrooms. They're trying to figure out what the benefits and problems might be.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have school-age grandchildren or run an education business, this shows schools are still deciding how to use AI safely with students.

stories.title: Artificial intelligence agents going rogue fuel calls for regulation
stories.simple_summary: Some AI programs are behaving in unexpected or unwanted ways, and people are calling for new rules to control them. It's like a tool that's doing things the owner didn't intend.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly affects tech companies and engineers right now — there's no immediate action needed for ordinary people.

stories.title: House Intelligence Committee warns of 'Black Swan' AI risks
stories.simple_summary: A congressional committee is warning that AI could cause a major, unexpected problem for society. Think of it like a car with brakes that might fail suddenly.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly a warning for lawmakers and investors — it doesn't mean AI is dangerous for you to use in your daily business today.

stories.title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
stories.simple_summary: The Pentagon (the US military) now has its own AI chat tools like ChatGPT, including ones made by military contractors. It's similar to how a large company builds custom software for its needs.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to government and defense industry workers — it's not relevant to ordinary small business owners.

stories.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
stories.simple_summary: Instagram is making AI profiles that aren't clearly labeled as AI have less visibility to users. The app wants people to know when they're talking to a computer, not a real person.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Instagram for business or personal reasons, this is good news — you'll see fewer fake AI accounts pretending to be real people.

stories.title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a ‘Harvey for police officers’
stories.simple_summary: A new company called Blue Voice is building AI software designed specifically for police officers, trained on local laws and department rules. It's like a very specialized AI assistant instead of a general one.
stories.why_it_matters: Unless you work in law enforcement, this doesn't affect you — it's a specialized tool for police use only.

stories.title: Your boss, tech companies and police can read your chatbot conversations
stories.simple_summary: When you type into a chatbot, your boss, tech companies, and sometimes police can read what you wrote. Your conversations aren't as private as you might think.
stories.why_it_matters: Be careful about what personal or sensitive business information you share in free chatbot tools — treat them like they're being read by others.

stories.title: AI could cause global economic downturn, Andrew Bailey warns G20
stories.simple_summary: A top official from the Bank of England warned other countries that AI could hurt the world's economy and cause a downturn. It's a warning that AI could cause serious economic problems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly economic analysis for policymakers — it doesn't mean you should stop using AI tools in your business right now.

stories.title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M
stories.simple_summary: A company that uses AI to search through huge amounts of video files very quickly is now worth $250 million. It's become a valuable business because it solves a real problem.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — it shows that specialized AI tools can become profitable, but it won't change how you work today.

stories.title: Debian won’t ban AI code from its Linux distribution
stories.simple_summary: The Debian project (a type of free computer software) decided to allow programmers to use AI tools to help them write code and documentation. They say responsible AI use can help developers work better.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to software engineers — it won't affect you unless you work in computer programming.
